title: Hosted API demo: embeddings + rerank - Acme Corp
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Acme through hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints for improving search relevance. Discussed integration paths (API + Console), latency vs cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2, KMS), and suggested pilot/benchmarks. Customer interested in a 2-week POC to validate improvement on product search and to measure latency under typical queries.
next_steps: Sasha - share pricing + starter POC plan by 2027-02-25
Jordan - provide sample benchmark script and embed/rerank example repo by 2027-02-26
Acme - provide sample dataset (top 10k product queries) by 2027-02-28
action_items: Sasha - Send pricing and trial details by 2027-02-25
Jordan - Upload example jumpstart script and small benchmark harness by 2027-02-26
Tom - Share current embeddings vector spec and 1k sample queries by 2027-02-28
transcript:
[00:00:00] Sasha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh gonna get started in a minute. Looks like we have Lena, Tom and Priya from Acme, Jordan from our side is the SE - he'll run through the deep bits.  
[00:00:18] Lena (Acme): Yeah hi thanks, apologies for being on weird wifi - I might drop, hope not. We're excited to see the embeddings + rerank flow; search relevance has been tough.
[00:00:30] Jordan (Redwood SE): Cool, quick agenda - show hosted embeddings endpoint, then the rerank endpoint and how it plugs into your search stack, demo in the Console, then Q&A and next steps. I'll try to keep things light on the slides.
[00:00:45] Tom (Acme): Quick qual - we currently use OpenSearch with custom BM25 + a Pinecone vector layer for semantic. Latency target is sub 120ms for web queries, and cost needsto be reasonable, we can't blow budget.
[00:01:05] Sasha: Got it, yeah most customers use a hybrid approach. For hosted API we provide embeddings as a managed endpoint, and a separate rerank endpoint that accepts a query + candidate docs and returns scores - so you can keep BM25 for candidate recall and then rerank top-K.
[00:01:30] Jordan: Demo time - share screen - (screen share noises) - here's Console, route created for "acme-product-search" pointing at hosted-embed-prod model. Example request: POST /v1/embeddings with payload text: "red running shoes"; response returns a 1536-dim vector (note: dims and model vary by model selection).
[00:01:58] Priya (Acme): Sorry quick - how do we handle keys and where are vectors stored? We currently keep vectors in Pinecone but want optional managed storage.
[00:02:12] Sasha: For hosted, we do not persist your raw text for the embeddings unless you opt into retention. Vectors can be returned and you store them in your index (Pinecone/Weaviate/Elastic) - we also have optional managed vector stores as an add-on. Keys are via our Console or API keys, and we support KMS-integrations for enterprise.
[00:02:35] Tom: And SSO / RBAC?
[00:02:40] Jordan: Yep SSO SAML/SCIM available on enterprise, RBAC in Console, audit logs. We also have SOC2 report and ISO stuff - Sasha will share security pack.
[00:02:55] Lena: Great. Show rerank please.
[00:03:05] Jordan: Rerank endpoint - you send a query and an array of candidate doc texts or ids plus embeddings; Redwood can accept either raw text or embeddings to avoid double-embedding; the rerank model is optimized to be cheaper because it operates on smaller candidate sets so it's cost-efficient vs just generating large cross-encoder calls for everything. Example: POST /v1/rerank body { query:..., candidates:[{id:.., text:..}] } returns scored list.
[00:03:35] Sasha: Important nuance: our rerank supports both hosted-mode where vectors are computed server-side, and fast path where you pass precomputed embeddings to avoid repeating costs. That is useful when you already manage a vector index.
[00:03:50] Tom: Latency numbers?
[00:03:55] Jordan: For rerank on top-10 candidates we typically see 20-80ms p95 on dedicated pools; on hosted shared pools p95 can be 60-200ms depending on model and sequence lengths. There's tradeoffs - smaller models faster/cheaper, larger models better at semantic nuance.
[00:04:18] Lena: Our queries vary, many short product names but sometimes long descriptions with attributes. Does KV cache help?
[00:04:25] Jordan: Yes, caching for prefix patterns and hot items reduces token compute; also batching on our runtime helps throughput during spikes. Console shows token-level cost breakdown so you can tune.
[00:04:40] Priya: How about private data: we must keep PII out and have traffic egress rules - we need VPC or on-prem eventually.
[00:04:48] Sasha: Private deployment available, we offer VPC connectors and on-prem packages for regulated cases. For initial POC hosted is fine with KMS and retention controls.
[00:05:05] Marco (PM): Any libraries / quickstart code?
[00:05:10] Jordan: Yes we have SDKs in Python/Node and example repos. I'll drop a repo link after the call. Note: some auto- transcripts might spell things odd but code links will be exact.
[00:05:25] [Demo continues - Jordan shows a live rerank call against a toy dataset - slight audio glitch at 00:06:10 - transcription may miss a few words]
[00:06:30] Jordan: Here's an example where we pass precomputed candidate embeddings to the rerank endpoint. It avoids recomputing and gives you the fastest path. Code: client.rerank.create({ query: 'black waterproof jacket', candidates: [{id: 'p1', embedding: [...]}, ...] }) -> returns ranked ids with scores.
[00:07:02] Tom: The embedding dims you returned earlier - we use 512 dims currently and storage is tuned for that, will switching models change costs?
[00:07:15] Sasha: It can; higher-dimension vectors cost more to store and more compute for similarity. We usually recommend 1536 for higher quality models but you can quantize or use smaller models. Redwood Optimize includes recommendations for quantization/profiles by workload.
[00:07:35] Lena: Any A/B testing or rollouts? We want to try rerank on a subset of queries.
[00:07:42] Jordan: Console supports route-level rollouts - canary to 10%, A/B test, automatic fallback to BM25 if latency or quality dips. We also emit eval metrics tied to prompt sets so you can set regression alerts.
[00:08:00] Priya: If we do a POC, how do we benchmark?
[00:08:05] Jordan: We usually run a 1-2 week benchmark: export 10k queries, pick top-K candidates via current retrieval, run rerank with Redwood, measure MRR/CTR/loss and latency. I'll provide a small harness script that hits hosted endpoints with concurrency to estimate p95.
[00:08:25] Sasha: We'll also include a cost estimate based on token counts and rerank calls per query. Typical customers saw 15-30% improvement in relevance with rerank on product search in our internal case studies.
[00:08:42] Lena: That's promising, the product team will be pleased. Any major blockers we should be aware of?
[00:08:50] Tom: Data residency - some EU customers require vector storage in region.
[00:08:55] Sasha: We have region routing and can pin routes to specific regions; for full residency you'd look at Private or Dedicated. We'll call out options in the security pack.
[00:09:10] Marco: Cost controls - do you do quotas/alerts?
[00:09:14] Jordan: Yes per-route quotas, rate limits, and cost alerts in Console. You can also configure fallback policies to cheaper models automatically.
[00:09:25] [Small cross talk about demo visuals, Jordan scrolls through Console logs and token breakdowns]
[00:09:50] Lena: Ok on integration side, how long before we can get a working POC? We're aiming for a quick win by mid-March.
[00:09:58] Sasha: If you can provide 1k-10k sample queries and candidate sets we'll set up a 2-week POC starting the first week of March, engineer bandwidth permitting. Jordan can help define the harness.
[00:10:12] Tom: One more Q - our infra team wants to run local benchmarks to compare throughput vs our current Pinecone vector-only pipeline. Can we get a sandbox account with some rate limits?
[00:10:23] Sasha: Yep sandbox keys + rate-limited accounts for POC. We'll supply credentials scoped to the POC.
[00:10:35] Priya: Also need SOC2 and third-party pen test results.
[00:10:40] Sasha: I'll share SOC2 and the security pack after the call.
[00:10:45] [00:10:45-00:25:00 - Jordan walks through example API call patterns, shows Node/Python snippets, some transcription dropped at 00:12:50 due to network]
[00:25:05] Jordan: Now quick demo of rerank tuning - show how weights and feature signals can be added (e.g. recency boost, price match) combined with model score. You can do hybrid scoring: weighted sum of BM25+model_score+business_signals.
[00:25:30] Lena: Can we surface model explainability or why an item was boosted?
[00:25:35] Jordan: We offer score breakdowns and a lightweight rationale output for some models, but it's not full feature attribution. It's mostly "model_score:0.8, recency:0.1, price_match:0.05" - human-readable decodes.
[00:25:55] Tom: Any gotchas with throughput under peak traffic?
[00:26:00] Jordan: Batching and autoscaling help; for high QPS we recommend Dedicated capacity. Hosted can burst but may have higher p95 under extreme spikes. For production, many customers start hosted for POC then move to Dedicated when they need guaranteed SLOs.
[00:26:20] Lena: Ok that's consistent with our infra plan.
[00:26:25] Jordan: Let's recap next steps: Sasha will send pricing and SOC2, Jordan will share code and benchmark script, Acme to provide dataset, schedule kickoff.
[00:26:40] Sasha: Any other technical blockers?
[00:26:45] Priya: Not yet; will review security pack and come back.
[00:26:50] Marco: We'll loop in product analytics for evaluation metrics.
[00:26:55] Sasha: Great. Thanks everyone - should we book a 30m POC kickoff for March 1st?
[00:27:05] Lena: Yes please.
[00:27:08] Tom: Thanks all.
[00:27:12] [Wrap up small talk, call ends around 15:45 UTC - recording likely cut at 15:45:20 - some timestamps in transcript approximate]
